extracted.intended_audience: AmeriCorps stakeholders (State Commissions, current and prospective AmeriCorps Seniors grantees/sponsors), nonprofit and for-profit volunteer station operators, policy commenters, and members of the public invited to submit regulatory comments
extracted.subtask_description: An Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) soliciting public comment on four specific regulatory prohibitions/requirements affecting AmeriCorps Seniors programs (State Commission operation, grantee delegation/contracting, for‑profit childcare as volunteer sites, and insurance requirements). The document asks whether each prohibition/requirement should be retained, modified, or removed and explains historical context and possible effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on State Commissions Operating AmeriCorps Seniors Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: State Commissions are prohibited by regulation from directly carrying out any national service program under title II of the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973, as amended (DVSA), 45 CFR 2550.80(j). Together with provisions prohibiting delegation/contracting of overall management responsibilities, these restrictions effectively create a categorical ban on State Commissions being AmeriCorps Seniors grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background and history: there is no statutory prohibition on State Commissions operating AmeriCorps Seniors programs (statutory prohibition applies to ASN grants only). In 1993 the prohibition was expanded by regulation to include AmeriCorps Seniors; in 2005 AmeriCorps removed VISTA from the prohibition but retained it for Seniors. Past justifications included that without delegation/subgrant authority State Commissions could not operate programs and that local organizations were best positioned to identify needs; the agency reported no indication Commissions wanted to operate. Since then, some State Commissions have shown interest and some operate under waivers. AmeriCorps requests public input on whether to retain, modify, or remove the regulatory prohibition on State Commissions directly operating AmeriCorps Seniors programs and the reasoning for retaining/modifying/removing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on AmeriCorps Seniors Grantees Delegating or Contracting Overall Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Current regulations require AmeriCorps Seniors grantees to fulfill all project management requirements necessary to accomplish the purposes of the program and prohibit them from delegating or contracting (i.e., subcontracting) the overall management responsibilities to another entity (see 45 CFR 2551.22, 2552.22, 2553.22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential impacts and rationale for reconsideration: removing the general prohibition could allow small grantees to obtain outside experts for financial management (recordkeeping, accounting, internal controls), potentially reducing audit/monitoring findings, freeing staff to focus on programmatic goals, and increasing State Commissions' ability to operate programs. The regulations currently also provide AmeriCorps flexibility to determine what management responsibilities may or may not be contracted. AmeriCorps seeks public comment on whether and why to retain, modify, or remove the prohibition on delegating or contracting management duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on For‑Profit Childcare or Educational Centers Serving as Volunteer Stations for Foster Grandparents
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors in the Foster Grandparent Program must develop and manage volunteer stations that are public or non‑profit private organizations or eligible proprietary health care agencies (see 45 CFR 2552.23(c)(1) and 2552.12). Proprietary health care organizations (private, for‑profit health care organizations serving vulnerable populations) have been allowed since before 1983 and were defined in 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed consideration: AmeriCorps Seniors is considering adding a similar allowance for proprietary childcare organizations, defined as private, for‑profit childcare or child‑education organizations that serve one or more vulnerable populations with a high percentage of those populations represented among children/families served. Rationale: in some communities there are no nonprofit childcare organizations but there are for‑profit centers, and allowing them to serve as volunteer stations could expand services to children in need. Questions for comment include whether to add for‑profit childcare organizations to eligible volunteer station types, whether they should be eligible only when no nonprofit childcare organizations exist in or near the community, and whether there is any basis for continuing to exclude them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Insurance for AmeriCorps Seniors Grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Current regulations require grantees (sponsors) to provide appropriate coverage for AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers, including accident insurance, personal liability insurance, and excess automobile liability insurance (see 45 CFR 2551.25, 2552.25, 2553.25). The regulations explain each insurance type and allow reimbursement of costs associated with the insurance if grantees maintain the insurance at minimum levels set by AmeriCorps (see 45 CFR 2551.46(b), 2552.46(b), 2553.46(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose and tradeoffs: these insurance requirements are intended to help protect volunteers and grantees in the event of accidents or injuries during service. However, insurance is not required by statute and some grantees find it challenging to secure. AmeriCorps seeks public comment on whether to remove the requirement for grantees to obtain insurance while retaining insurance premiums as allowable reimbursable costs if grantees choose to obtain the listed insurance types.
